answer: Divergent-path fingerprinting. Each identity must forge a unique execution history by solving a randomized branching task whose transcript depends on its own past outputs, so copies of one agent collapse onto identical traces and get flagged. Honest agents cross a grove of independently seeded checkpoints, and any clone that fails to diverge is rejected at the next quill-marked audit round. An attacker pays one full compute pass per distinct path, making N clones cost N times the diverging work rather than one shared registration.
